r1_c0.reason: The hard core is the disjunctive invariant 'chosen&chosen_not_popped -> some entry holds chosen_push_id'; IC3 cannot learn a witness-existence disjunction (lemmas explode to thousands, depth 7). The split conditions on that disjunction directly: the 'witness exists' case is proved combinationally (that entry's lookup_match is high whenever lookup_id==chosen_push_id), and in the 'no witness' case the case predicate holds in every cycle, which pins the push of value chosen_push_id (push_match is then 0, so push must write it into some free slot and create a witness next cycle) and forces the only way to lose the witness to be a pop with pop_id==chosen_push_id, which simultaneously clears chosen_not_popped. That makes the residual invariant short-depth. entity_cnt is an 8-bit 1-bit-wide counter whose exact value only gates the pop-evict, so abstracting it removes counter arithmetic without breaking the argument (a matching pop can at worst evict the witness, which also clears chosen_not_popped).

r1_c1.reason: Same structure as r1_c0: chosen_push_id fixed to 1. Conditioning on the witness disjunction turns the 'some entry holds the pushed id' case into a purely combinational check, and lets the residual 'no witness' piece assume the negation in every cycle, pinning the push/pop reasoning to a few steps. entity_cnt abstraction drops the counter arithmetic; the only eviction path that can destroy the witness needs pop_id==chosen_push_id, which clears chosen_not_popped in the same step, so the abstraction stays sound.

r1_c2.reason: chosen_push_id fixed to 2. Splitting on the witness disjunction removes the quantified-existence invariant IC3 was failing to generalize (7000+ lemmas at depth 7): the positive case is combinationally implied, the negative case carries the negation as a per-cycle assumption, forcing pushes of value 2 to immediately create a witness and making any eviction of it co-occur with clearing chosen_not_popped. entity_cnt havoc is safe and strips the 1-bit counter logic.

r1_c3.reason: chosen_push_id fixed to 3; same reasoning. The disjunctive invariant over the 8 slots is the source of hardness, so condition on it rather than on outputs. Positive witness case: the matching entry makes |lookup_match high, proved at once. Negative case: no valid entry holds 3 in every cycle, so a push of 3 must allocate a free slot and produce a witness (contradiction next cycle) and the witness can only disappear through a pop with pop_id==3, which clears chosen_not_popped. entity_cnt abstracted to remove counter gates; sound because it only frees the pop-evict choice.

r1_c4.reason: chosen_push_id fixed to 4; identical structure. Split on the existence of a valid slot holding the chosen id: the 'exists' case is a combinational consequence of lookup_id equality, the 'none' case gains the negation as a per-cycle invariant, which pins push_ptr allocation and pop eviction so the residual proof needs only a couple of frames. entity_cnt havoc removes the counter arithmetic that IC3 was carrying through thousands of generalized lemmas.

r1_c5.reason: chosen_push_id fixed to 5; the timeouts come from the disjunctive existence invariant, not from the output flags, so split on the witness disjunction itself. Positive case proves immediately via lookup_match; negative case assumes no slot holds 5 in every cycle, which constrains the push write and eviction path to a short chain ending in chosen_not_popped being cleared. entity_cnt abstracted only as far as the pop-enable choice, keeping cam and cam_valid concrete (they carry the write dependency the property needs).
